text:
ryan: Heads-up - after today's NF4 canary push on pool-C we see ~18-25% throughput drop and a sharp memory climb before requests start failing. p99 latency spikes. perf-bot posted traces. :eyes:

perf-bot: telemetry snapshot for pool-C:
kernel_path=nv-flex-slow | qformat=NF4 | p50=34ms | p95=120ms | p99=300ms | tput=1200rps (-22% vs baseline)

tanvi: Any kv-cache evictions/GC spikes?

ryan: yes - kv slab fragmentation and eviction rate jumps right before the throughput dip. Seen on 3/6 hosts in pool-C. Attaching trimmed profiler snippet below (stack sampling).

ryan: ```
# kernel selector log excerpt
[13:41:02] selector: chosen=nv-flex-slow for model=redwood/nf4-small seq=2048
[13:41:02] fallback: scalar_ref (latency penalty) for seq>1024 and qformat=NF4
[13:41:15] kv: slab_frag=0.72 eviction_rate=120/s
[13:41:20] mem.used=18.2GB -> 24.6GB in 18s
```

tanvi: hmm, fallback to scalar_ref for long sequences would explain p99. Why is selector choosing nv-flex-slow? It should prefer nv-fused if available. Any recent changes?

sam: batching heuristics were tweaked in the same deploy (merge 0x1a2b) to prefer larger micro-batches for NF4 to improve throughput. Could be interaction causing longer-lived KV entries and fragmentation. Also saw some CPU steal on those machines.

maria: Can we get the kernel-selection table for the canary hosts? Maybe the kernel scoring function misweights memory cost vs perf. If it's choosing a slower codepath with lower memory headroom it could trigger KV churn.

ryan: pasted selector table from host-17:
```
kernel_score: nv-fused=0.82, nv-flex-fast=0.76, nv-flex-slow=0.78, scalar_ref=0.50
reason: nv-fused disabled (compat flag false) -> comparator picks nv-flex-slow due to lower estimated mem delta for NF4
```

ops: rolling back the kernel-selector tweak on pool-C now (rollback-id 2026-rc-rollback-17). Will monitor telemetry; ETA ~8m. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: rollback triggered by ops at 13:58:12. New telemetry expected in ~5m.

maria: Proposed next steps:
- Bisect kernel-selector change + the batching heuristics change (they landed together).
- Add guard to prefer fused kernels for NF4 when present (explicit override).
- Temporarily relax KV slab defrag interval to reduce churn (30s -> 5m) while we investigate.
- Add histogram metrics for slab occupancy and per-tenant eviction bursts.

ryan: agree. I'll run a targeted perf job that simulates mixed sequence lengths (50% long 2048, 50% short 128) with NF4 path to reproduce. Will also capture heap profiles and kernel trace. Tagging @tanvi for KV instrumentation.

tanvi: on it - will add slab occupancy histogram and per-slab eviction counters. Also will emit event when slab_frag > 0.6.

sam: small local repro that shows the p99 jump: `ab-run --model=redwood/nf4-small --seq=2048,128 --mix=50:50 --concurrency=64`

ryan: thanks. After rollback telemetry looks like p99 and tput are trending back to baseline on the rolled hosts. If stable for 10m we'll promote rollback to stable until we have a root-cause.

maria: agree - let's not ship the selector change until we have the bisect results. Also adding a test to CI that runs mixed-seq workloads on NF4 kernels to catch regressions.

ops: rollback held and flagged. Will open a ticket and link logs. ticket: INF-4729.

ryan: filing perf ticket now and attaching profiler + kernel selector diff. :white_check_mark:
